entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Al-Mufaddal ibn Abi al-Fada'il was a 14th-century Egyptian historian who was a Coptic Christian.

Born in unknown year, he rose to prominence as a prolific writer and scholar in the Islamic world, producing works that showcased his expertise in Arabic literature and history.

His most notable achievement was the compilation of the book 'Tarikh al-Mamluk,' which chronicled the history of the Mamluk Sultanate, a powerful Islamic dynasty that ruled Egypt and Syria from the 13th to the 16th century.

This work not only provided valuable insights into the Mamluk period but also helped to establish Al-Mufaddal as a leading figure in Egyptian historiography.

Despite his significant contributions to the field of history, Al-Mufaddal's work has largely been overlooked in Western scholarship, making him a fascinating subject for reevaluation.

He died in 1358, leaving behind a legacy of scholarship and cultural transmission that continues to inspire historians and scholars today.

Al-Mufaddal's work has been recognized for its significance in the preservation of Arabic literature and its role in shaping the cultural identity of Egypt during the Mamluk period.
